Toy list of missing taxa, with allowed states of two traits: colors and elevation

Source: R/dataset_doc.R
toy_missing_taxa_list_with_two_traits.Rd

Same as phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list, with the extra item $allowed_states covering the states of two traits, phylograftR::toy_simmap ("blue", "green", "red") and phylograftR::toy_simmap_elevation ("high", "low"), in which each taxon can be grafted. It is used to showcase the grafting constrained by several traits at once (see Several traits in Details section of phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa()).

It is the output of phylograftR::import_missing_taxa_list() applied to the table system.file("extdata", "toy_missing_taxa_with_two_traits.csv", package = "phylograftR"). In the column allowed_states, the states of the traits are separated by semicolons (in the order of the maps provided in simmap: the color, then the elevation), and the states of a trait by commas. Open that file to see the different syntaxes:

  • "red;": the color is "red", and the elevation has no taxon-level value (the global value is used).

  • "blue, green;high": color "blue" or "green", and elevation "high".

  • ";low": no taxon-level value for the color, elevation "low".

  • "elevation=high": traits named, so the color can be omitted (it has no taxon-level value).

  • Blank cell: no taxon-level value for any trait, so the global allowed_states argument is used for both.

Usage

data(toy_missing_taxa_list_with_two_traits)

Format

A named list with the same 7 taxa and items as phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list, and the extra item:

  • $allowed_states List (one element per taxon, named after the taxa) of lists with the states of each trait (one element per trait, NULL for a trait without taxon-level value), or NULL to use the global allowed_states argument for all the traits. "New_sp1": list("red", NULL); "New_sp4": list(c("blue", "green"), "high"); "New_sp5": list(NULL, "low"); "New_sp7": list(elevation = "high"); the others: NULL.

See also

Other datasets and functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_states for the same list, with allowed states of colors.

  • phylograftR::toy_simmap for the stochastic character map of colors.

  • phylograftR::toy_simmap_elevation for the stochastic character map of elevation.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() to graft taxa within a target clade based on colors and elevation, using this dataset.

# Import the list
data(toy_missing_taxa_list_with_two_traits)
toy_missing_taxa_list_with_two_traits$allowed_states

#> 
#> 

# Compare to the initial '.csv' file
system.file("extdata", "toy_missing_taxa_with_two_traits.csv", package = "phylograftR")
#> [1] "/home/runner/.cache/R/renv/library/phylograftR-802cedf8/linux-ubuntu-resolute/R-4.6/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/phylograftR/extdata/toy_missing_taxa_with_two_traits.csv"

# Graft with the maps of the two traits. The global 'allowed_states' has one element per trait:
# grafting on "blue" or "green" branches for the color, and no restriction for the elevation (NULL).
data(toy_backbone)
data(toy_simmap)
data(toy_simmap_elevation)

grafted_phy <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = toy_backbone,
    missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list_with_two_traits,
    simmap = list(color = toy_simmap, elevation = toy_simmap_elevation),
    allowed_states = list(c("blue", "green"), NULL),
    verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)

# One updated simmap per trait
names(grafted_phy$simmap)
#> [1] "color"     "elevation"

# State of each grafted taxon for each trait: should match the allowed states
taxon_names <- toy_missing_taxa_list_with_two_traits$Taxon_name
taxon_states <- sapply(grafted_phy$simmap, function (simmap)
{
  tip_edges <- match(match(taxon_names, simmap$tip.label), simmap$edge[, 2])
  setNames(vapply(simmap$maps[tip_edges], function (x) names(x)[1], character(1)), taxon_names)
})
